title: Translate FunctionResult so a function returns its graph value, not T()
body:
## Summary
A Blueprint function body always ends `return T();` and its K2Node_FunctionResult is refused as having no translation rule, so the value the graph returns is dropped.

## Description
`generateCppFromBlueprint` appends `return false | nullptr | T()` after every non-void body (src/lib/blueprint-cpp-codegen.ts, function-implementation loop), regardless of what feeds the result pin. The walker reaches the FunctionResult node and falls into the generic branch (`no translation rule for node type`). Fixed: a FunctionResult whose return pin resolves via `resolveInputExpression` emits `return <expr>;` and is `emitted`; otherwise refused with the reason; a void result is structural; the trailing default return stays only when no return was emitted.

## Flow
- transpile a function Entry -> Result where the Result return pin is fed by a VariableGet of Score
- observed: body `// TODO: [K2Node_FunctionResult] ...` then `return int32();`
- fix: a FunctionResult branch in walkNode using resolveInputExpression

## Expected impact
Every transpiled getter returns a default instead of its value, and the fidelity readout counts each FunctionResult as refused residue. Risk: codegen tests that pin `return int32();` (src/__tests__/lib/blueprint-cpp-codegen.test.ts:155) need re-pinning.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - transpiled functions return the value the graph returns
Before: Get Score fixture (blueprint-cpp-codegen.test.ts:155) emits `return int32();`; every FunctionResult is refused
After: predicted: `return Score;` for a VariableGet-fed result; void result structural
Method: simulation - walked the walker branches by hand; test not written this round (budget)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/lib/blueprint-cpp-codegen.ts: if (returnType !== "void") sourceLines.push(`\treturn ${... `${returnType}()`};`)
walkNode default branch: recordDisposition(ledger, node.id, "refused", `no translation rule for node type "${node.type}"`)
instrument: vitest: function graph Entry->Result with the Result input pin linked to a VariableGet; assert source contains `return Score;` and the ledger marks the result emitted

title: Semantic diff states rung declared-and-defined without reading a definition
body:
## Summary
computeSemanticDiff always reports fidelityRung `declared-and-defined`, but it only runs parseHeader over the pasted C++ and never checks a .cpp definition.

## Description
src/lib/blueprint-semantic-diff.ts:346 hardcodes `fidelityRung: "declared-and-defined"` and its comment claims the diff can show both sides DECLARE and DEFINE the same members. The C++ side is `parseHeader(existingCpp)` (line 96) - declarations only. The overwrite review already has a definition scanner (`definedNames`, src/lib/blueprint-transpiler/overwrite-review.ts:90). Fixed: derive the rung from what was inspected (a declaration-level rung for header-only input), or check definitions with definedNames when source is present. Registry visual-script-to-code-transpilation: a claim is stated only at the rung it was proven at.

## Flow
- paste a header with no .cpp into Semantic Diff
- observed: DiffPane shows Rung: declared-and-defined
- fix: rung from inspected dimensions; definition presence when a .cpp is present

## Expected impact
The rung chip stops overstating what the comparison proved. Risk: FidelityRung is an in-tree contract (DiffPane, tests) - needs a verifier.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the rung matches what was inspected
Before: header-only input -> declared-and-defined (0 definition reads, blueprint-semantic-diff.ts:96,346)
After: header-only input -> declaration-level rung; definitions checked when a .cpp is present
Method: simulation - read the code path; the ladder has no declared-only rung, so the right value is a type decision
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence:
src/lib/blueprint-semantic-diff.ts:96 const parsed = parseHeader(existingCpp);
src/lib/blueprint-semantic-diff.ts:346 fidelityRung: "declared-and-defined",
instrument: vitest: computeSemanticDiff(asset, headerOnly).fidelityRung is not declared-and-defined; with a matching .cpp missing a definition, a change is reported

title: blueprintTypeToCpp mis-splits a nested Map at the wrong comma
body:
## Summary
The Map regex uses a greedy first group, so `Map<string, Map<int,bool>>` splits at the inner comma and both halves pass through unmapped.

## Description
src/lib/blueprint-parser.ts Map branch matches `(.+)\s*,\s*(.+)` greedily: the first group backtracks to the LAST comma, giving key `string, Map<int` and value `bool>`; both miss every branch and return as-is, so the header gets `TMap<string, Map<int, bool>>` (no FString, no inner TMap/int32). Fixed: split on the top-level comma by bracket depth.

## Flow
- Blueprint variable of type Map<string, Map<int,bool>>
- observed: `TMap<string, Map<int, bool>> X;`
- fix: depth-aware top-level comma split

## Expected impact
Nested-container variables get valid C++ types. Risk: low, pure function with existing tests.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - nested map types map recursively
Before: walked: Map<string, Map<int,bool>> -> TMap<string, Map<int, bool>>
After: predicted TMap<FString, TMap<int32, bool>>
Method: simulation - regex walked by hand; not executed this round
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Two more highlight() callers leak an unhandled rejection
body:
## Summary
CodeBlockHighlighter and the ability CodePreview call `highlight(...).then(...)` with no rejection handler; b0d2767c fixed only CodeViewer and the singleton.

## Description
src/components/cli/CodeBlockHighlighter.tsx:60 and src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ability/blueprint/CodePreview.tsx:27 chain `.then` only. A failed Shiki init surfaces as one unhandled rejection per mounted block. Both files are outside this round's paths (CLI and ability contexts).

## Flow
- shiki chunk fails to load once
- observed: unhandled promise rejection per CLI code block
- fix: the same no-op rejection handler (the plain fallback already renders)

## Expected impact
No unhandled-rejection noise in the CLI transcript. Risk: none.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - highlight failures handled at every caller
Before: 1 of 3 highlight() callers handles rejection (grep `highlight(` with .then)
After: 3 of 3
Method: probe - grep over src/**/*.tsx; out-of-scope files so not built
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: component test mocking highlight to reject; assert no unhandled rejection and the plain <pre> stays

title: Text pins emit TEXT() into FText arguments, which does not compile
body:
## Summary
renderPinLiteral quotes `text` pins as `TEXT("...")`; FText has no conversion from a TCHAR literal, so a call taking FText gets an argument that does not compile.

## Description
src/lib/blueprint-cpp-codegen.ts STRING_PIN_TYPES includes `text` and renders it via cppStringLiteral as `TEXT("...")`. 0180bba9 refused this for UPROPERTY defaults (renderPropertyDefault); pin arguments still emit it. Fixed: text pins render `FText::FromString(TEXT("..."))` (or INVTEXT), or are refused.

## Flow
- CallFunction with an FText input pin carrying a literal
- observed: `Foo(TEXT("Hi"));` against an FText parameter
- fix: a text-specific literal

## Expected impact
Calls with FText arguments compile. Risk: the test at src/__tests__/lib/blueprint-cpp-codegen.test.ts:733 (quotes text pins) needs re-pinning.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - FText arguments compile
Before: text pin -> TEXT("...") (pinned by test :733)
After: FText::FromString(TEXT("...")) or a refusal
Method: simulation - UE FText has no TCHAR* constructor; nothing compiled this round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/lib/blueprint-cpp-codegen.ts: const STRING_PIN_TYPES = new Set(["string", "text", "name"]); ... if (STRING_PIN_TYPES.has(type)) return { ok: true, code: cppStringLiteral(raw) };
instrument: vitest: renderPinLiteral({ name: "T", type: "text", direction: "input", defaultValue: "Hi" }) does not return a bare TEXT( literal

title: findJargonInText has no production consumer but its O(K^3) index runs on load
body:
## Summary
blueprint-jargon computes AMBIGUOUS_KEYS (each key against every key pair) at module load for findJargonInText, which only a test calls.

## Description
src/lib/blueprint-jargon.ts:362-392 builds AMBIGUOUS_KEYS / REGEX_KEYS / JARGON_REGEX at import; grep shows findJargonInText referenced only from src/__tests__/lib/blueprint-jargon.test.ts. The module is imported by TermChip, JargonTerm and crash-glossary, so every surface showing a term chip pays the init. Fixed: compute lazily on first call, or delete the function with its test if no surface needs it.

## Flow
- import TermChip anywhere
- observed: K x K x K substring scan at module evaluation
- fix: memoise on first findJargonInText call

## Expected impact
Lower module-eval cost for every term-chip surface. Risk: none if lazy.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - no eager O(K^3) init for an unused function
Before: 0 production consumers (grep); init time not taken (vitest probe printed nothing)
After: init deferred to first call
Method: probe - consumer count measured; the time delta is the open instrument
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
grep findJargonInText src -> src/lib/blueprint-jargon.ts and src/__tests__/lib/blueprint-jargon.test.ts only
src/lib/blueprint-jargon.ts:362 const AMBIGUOUS_KEYS = JARGON_KEYS.filter((k) => JARGON_KEYS.some((a) => { ... JARGON_KEYS.some((b) => {
instrument: performance.now() around a cold import of @/lib/blueprint-jargon in node, eager vs lazy, median of 20 runs

title: Semantic diff never checks the event overrides the Blueprint becomes
body:
## Summary
The surface resolves overrides (BeginPlay/Tick/EndPlay) but computeSemanticDiff compares only properties and UFUNCTIONs, so a header missing the BeginPlay the graph drives diffs clean.

## Description
deriveCppSurface returns `overrides` (src/lib/blueprint-cpp-surface.ts:204-218); computeSemanticDiff iterates surface.properties and surface.functions only (src/lib/blueprint-semantic-diff.ts:111, 215). NOT_COMPARED discloses node logic, not override presence. Fixed: an override-presence dimension (parseHeader would need virtual-override capture, or a scan like definedNames).

## Flow
- Blueprint with BeginPlay logic; C++ header without a BeginPlay override
- observed: overallConflict none (in compared dimensions)
- fix: an event-scoped change when an expected override is absent

## Expected impact
Drift where the C++ never runs the Blueprint startup logic becomes visible. Risk: parser extension in a shared parser.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - override drift detected
Before: 0 override checks in computeSemanticDiff
After: 1 change per missing override
Method: simulation - read both sides; whether parseHeader captures non-UFUNCTION virtuals is the build question
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/lib/blueprint-semantic-diff.ts:111 for (const prop of surface.properties)
src/lib/blueprint-semantic-diff.ts:215 for (const fn of surface.functions)
surface.overrides is never read
instrument: vitest: asset with a BeginPlay event + header lacking BeginPlay -> one change with scope event

title: Parent include covers 4 parents; any other base class gets none
body:
## Summary
Codegen adds a parent header only for ACharacter, APawn, AActor and components; a Blueprint whose parent is e.g. APlayerController gets a header with no include for its base.

## Description
src/lib/blueprint-cpp-codegen.ts (parent-include block after the duplicate-event loop) is an if/else over four parent names with no else. `class X : public APlayerController` with only CoreMinimal.h fails on an undefined base class. Fixed: a parent-to-header table for common engine bases, plus an error-severity warning naming the missing include for an unknown parent (refuse rather than emit silently).

## Flow
- transpile a Blueprint with ParentClass APlayerController
- observed: includes = [CoreMinimal.h, X.generated.h]
- fix: table + warning

## Expected impact
Generated headers for other bases compile, or say why not. Risk: low.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every generated header includes its base class
Before: 4 parent names handled; any other parent silent
After: common bases mapped; unknown parent warns
Method: simulation - read the branch; not compiled
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/lib/blueprint-cpp-codegen.ts: if (parentClass === "ACharacter" || parentClass === "Character") { ... } else if (isComponent) { includes.add("Components/ActorComponent.h"); }  // no else
instrument: vitest: parentClass APlayerController -> includes contains GameFramework/PlayerController.h, or a warning names the missing base include
